title: Apparently I Am Now the kingdom’s least qualified problem solver and the Demon King Sent Me an Invoice
synopsis: A failed office worker is reincarnated as a royal treasurer in a kingdom whose economy is governed by absurd laws. The story unfolds in The Moonlit Federation of Mostly Normal People, where moonlight reveals hidden contracts and temporary enchantments. The central problem is a missing royal relic that insists it was never missing. Yuna Locke wants to collect evidence before anyone notices the plot, but every reasonable solution creates a new unreasonable obligation.
premise: A failed office worker is reincarnated as a royal treasurer in a kingdom whose economy is governed by absurd laws.
authorNotes: The worldbuilding is extremely serious. The author is not.

world.oddity: The capital holds elections for positions nobody remembers creating.
world.magic: The oldest spells are bureaucratic procedures nobody remembers inventing.

chapters.title: I Regret Discovering the World's Least Useful Sword — Yuna Locke POV
chapters.arcTitle: The Problem With The Original Plan
paragraphs: CHAPTER 1 — Yuna Locke POV
The Problem With The Original Plan had already produced two meetings, one argument, and a document nobody could legally throw away.
Yuna Locke arrived at the eastern market intending to collect evidence before anyone notices the plot. The plan lasted until the first unexpected detail appeared.
A completely irrelevant item becomes the legal key to the crisis.
Yuna Locke knew, with the terrible certainty reserved for prophecies and overdue bills, that this moment mattered.
The important object was a permit. It was not magical in the usual sense, which made it considerably more suspicious.
Yuna Locke checked the obvious explanation first. It was wrong. They checked the ridiculous explanation next. It was unfortunately closer.
The world of The Moonlit Federation of Mostly Normal People followed one inconvenient rule: Moonlight reveals hidden contracts and temporary enchantments.
The irrelevant permit became relevant when an old law was quoted from memory and turned out to be correct.
Somewhere, history was preparing to make a poor decision.
A second person arrived carrying information about the anonymous letter writer. Their explanation contradicted the first explanation in exactly the way a useful clue should.
Nobody agreed on what to do with the permit. One person wanted to destroy it. Another wanted to file it. Yuna Locke wanted to know why it had appeared here.
That question led to a small discovery: Yuna Locke has a private connection to the oldest dungeon.
The mystery remained open, although Yuna Locke now had one useful fact: someone was treating the anonymous letter writer as if it were a normal administrative matter.
Before leaving, Yuna Locke made a decision that would matter later: they would not trust the next official document until they had read the footnotes.
For the first time that day, everyone agreed on something. This was probably going to get worse.
